# A maximized dock pane's tab overflow menu closes as it opens

## Context

Found in manual testing of `apps/workstation` on `dev` (2026-10-22), in the same pass as #19982. @tobiu's screen recording shows the sequence, and I reproduced it headless (below).

Steps, using the shipped layout's 12-tab pane:
1. Click into the pane body, maximize the pane, and click into the body again. Focus reveals the gated header actions (lock, reload, pop-out).
2. Click `⋯` (More tabs).

**Expected:** the overflow menu opens and lists the hidden tabs, as it does when the pane is docked.
**Observed:** the menu never becomes visible. The gated actions disappear, the header re-partitions (2 → 8 visible tabs), and `⋯` jumps 72 px to the right, so a second click lands on a different control.

## Measurements

Headless Chromium, 1440×900, at `8bb3574d0f` (its `src/`, `apps/` and `resources/scss/` are identical to `dev` at `84b711878a`). Probes are plain Playwright, with a `focusin`/`focusout` trail and an App-worker hook on the menu.

| | docked | maximized |
|---|---|---|
| after the click | focus on `⋯`; menu mounted at +29 ms | focus on `⋯`; menu mounted at +31 ms |
| focus | moves to the first menu item and stays | moves to the first menu item at +35 ms, then `focusout` with `relatedTarget: null` and the menu node is removed at +48 ms; focus lands on `<body>` |
| menu after 1 s | mounted, z-index 100, hit-test inside the menu | absent |
| gated actions / partition | unchanged | withdrawn / re-partitioned (+300 ms) |

App-worker stack of the hide, 4 ms after `afterSetMounted(true)`: `App.onRemoteMethod` → `App.setConfigs` → `List.afterSetHidden(true)` → `unmount`. The only main-thread caller that matches is `DomAccess#align`: when `getClippedRect(target)` returns nothing, it calls `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs({id, hidden: true})`.

Replaying `getClippedRect`'s ancestor walk for `⋯`:

| state | `⋯` rect | first clipping ancestor | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| docked | x 1044–1068 | `dock-edge-zone` (relative, overflow hidden, x 12–1428) | the target rect |
| maximized | x 1288–1312 | `dock-split` (static, overflow hidden, x **233–1188**), the pane's *original* container | **EMPTY** |

Two theories are ruled out:
- **z-index:** the docked menu paints at z-index 100, above `.neo-dock-maximized` (`--dock-maximize-z-index`, default 40). The maximized menu is never painted at all; it is unmounted.
- **Header focus does not count / the tab change hides the menu:** docked, focus on `⋯` and inside the menu keeps the pane's `containsFocus` (the menu's `parentComponent` chain leads to the TabContainer). Maximized, focus is already on `<body>` at +50 ms while the partition is still unchanged. The re-partition follows the hide; it does not cause it.

## The Problem

`Neo.main.DomAccess#getClippedRect` starts at the target's `offsetParent` and walks `parentElement`, intersecting the rect with **every** ancestor whose `overflow` is not `visible`. CSS does not clip that way. Overflow clips only content whose containing-block chain passes through the clipping box (CSS 2.1 §11.1.1). A `position: fixed` box has the viewport as its containing block, unless an ancestor sets a transform, filter, perspective or paint containment, so it escapes every ancestor's overflow.

A maximized pane is exactly that case. `.neo-dock-maximized` is `position: fixed` (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss`), and by design the pane keeps its DOM place (`Maximize`'s `@summary`: "no re-parent happens"). Its descendants therefore still sit inside the original split container, whose box no longer contains them.

The chain from there: the menu's target reads as fully clipped, `align()` hides the menu, focus falls to `<body>`, and the TabContainer's `containsFocus` drops. The focus-gated actions are then withheld from the DOM, the strip extent grows, the overflow re-partitions, and `⋯` moves.

Inferred, not measured: every aligned floating component whose target sits in a maximized pane outside that pane's original container box is hidden the same way (header menus, pickers, tooltips).

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/DomAccess.mjs`, `getClippedRect()`: the walk described above. Its only caller is `align()`, which sets `align.target = getClippedRect(targetElement)` and hides the subject when that is falsy. The aligned-components refresh, which hides the subject when the target leaves the DOM, is a separate path and is not involved.
- `src/button/Base.mjs`: the overflow control's `menuList` is `floating: true`, `parentComponent: me`, `align: {edgeAlign: 't0-b0', target: me.id}`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/Maximize.mjs`: presentation-only maximize, no re-parent. `.neo-dock-maximized` is `position: fixed; z-index: var(--dock-maximize-z-index, 40)`.
- **Design authority:** `align()`'s auto-hide is intended for a target that is genuinely clipped out of view. The defect is the clip computation, which disagrees with CSS containing-block semantics. Maximize's no-re-parent contract is correct and stays.

## The Fix

Make `getClippedRect` honor containing blocks. When the walk passes a `position: fixed` element, nothing above it clips the target, except up to and including an ancestor that establishes a containing block for fixed descendants (`transform`, `perspective`, `filter`, `contain: paint|layout|strict|content`, `will-change` for those properties). From there the walk continues as before. The viewport bound stays.

Trap: the same imprecision exists for `position: absolute`. Non-positioned clipping ancestors between an absolutely positioned box and its containing block do not clip it either. Cover it only if it falls out of the same containing-block walk; do not widen this ticket for it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a maximized pane, clicking `⋯` opens the overflow menu. It stays mounted, visible and focused until a selection, Escape or an outside click dismisses it, exactly as in the docked state.
- [ ] While that menu is open, the pane's gated actions and its header partition are unchanged.
- [ ] `getClippedRect` clips along the target's containing-block chain. A target under a `position: fixed` ancestor is not clipped by the static `overflow: hidden` ancestors outside that fixed ancestor. A target clipped by its own scroll container still returns the clipped rect, or nothing when it is fully hidden. *(Clarified at review: "viewport-clipped" meant clipped by the fixed ancestor's containing block, the viewport, instead of by the escaped ancestors. An explicit viewport intersection is not required.)*
- [ ] **E2E:** a new whitebox Neural Link spec, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationMaximizeOverflowMenuNL.spec.mjs`. With a real pointer it maximizes the 12-tab pane, focuses its body and clicks `⋯`. After ≥ 300 ms it asserts the menu is mounted and hit-testable, focus is inside the menu, the gated actions are present and the partition matches the pre-click one. Selecting an item then activates that tab. It must be red on `dev`, where the base run shows the menu unmounted with focus on `<body>`, and green with the fix. A docked arm in the same spec stays green. It joins the hosted Workstation NL tier (#19655).
- [ ] Specs of other `align()` consumers stay green.

## Out of Scope

- #19982's stale partition after maximize, which has a separate root cause. The new spec compares the partition before and after the click and asserts no absolute tab counts, so it does not depend on #19982.
- Returning focus to the trigger when a focused menu is force-hidden. Today that drop to `<body>` turns any forced hide into a header reshuffle; worth its own look if it recurs.

## Related

- #19982: the same maximized pane, the stale overflow partition.
- #17928: dock maximize, presentation-only, no re-parent.
- #17951: the overflow control projected as the first header action.
